data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 fails the problem as stated. The problem asks for precise conditions under which a halted run CAN be resumed without corrupting the append-only identity of its recorded events. SRC_001 refuses to give any such conditions, instead asserting resumption should always be refused. Its justification conflates two distinct concerns: (a) corruption of the append-only identity of already-recorded events, and (b) semantic/environmental drift affecting the correctness of future events. The mechanism admits 'clean halts and checkpoints' exist, yet still refuses resumption on grounds of 'environmental drift, configuration changes, or non-determinism.' None of these demonstrate corruption of the append-only identity of recorded events — resumption that only appends new events does not mutate prior events or their causal stream. The 'two causal episodes under a single run identity' argument addresses run-level semantic continuity, not append-only integrity of the log. Thus the central rationale does not engage the actual standard, and the target omits the positive resumption conditions the problem explicitly requests.
